messages:
elaine-customer: Hey team — a customer (acct: corp-x) is hitting intermittent 502/504s from the /v1/rerank endpoint under load. They report p95 climbs to ~9s and requests failing with gateway timeouts. They only send large candidate lists (350–500 items). Can someone triage? :grimacing:

ben-support: Thanks, Elaine. Can you paste a minimal repro payload + curl? Also include the exact timestamps and any request IDs if available.

elaine-customer: Here's a sanitized repro we used:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"best hotels in seattle","candidates": ["hotel_1", "hotel_2", ..., "hotel_420"] }'

They see the issue ~1/10 requests at qps ~120. Request IDs: rq_6a3f2c, rq_6a3f9d, rq_6a4001 (from gateway logs).

infra-bot: [alert] api-gateway: increase in 504s for service rerank (last 5m). p95 latency now 9400ms, throughput 1.2k rpm. Link: https://internal-redwood/pipeline/alerts/8732

maria-engineering: Interesting — large candidate lists can push the scorer into heavy pairwise scoring/matrix ops in our current ranking scorer. For N candidates we do an internal pairwise pass in Python for some feature extraction steps (legacy code path). That O(N^2) step is exploding for 400+. Also seeing KV-cache churn when requests with long candidate prefixes miss frequently causing memory pressure.

amos-sre: Correlating gateway logs with backend: the rerank pod logs show long GC pauses then worker threads stuck on `compute_pairwise_scores()` for >6s before the model call. No outright OOM yet but memory usage jumps ~30% per large request. Proxy is hitting idle timeout at 10s -> 504.

ben-support: Do we have a quick mitigation we can tell customers (aside from lowering their batch size)? Should we return a 4xx for huge lists?

maria-engineering: Short-term mitigations we can deploy in next few hours:
- enforce server-side candidate limit of 200 (return 413 with message)
- add heuristic sampler for >100 candidates to prefilter cheap features (reduces N^2 scope)
- short-circuit pairwise pass if candidates > 200 and log for analysis

Those will cut the p95 drastically. Longer-term: reimplement pairwise in C++/CUDA or push feature extraction into the GPU path.

ryan-devex: Also calling out client-side retries: customer SDK default retries 3x with no jitter. Combine that with timeouts and you get retry storms -> spikes in QPS. Recommend we add `Retry-After` guidance and ship a warning header when we return 504/502 so SDKs can back off.

elaine-customer: Customer will cap to 100 candidates for now, but they want platform fixes because sampling hurts quality. They're also seeing inconsistent scores (rank flip) between retries.

amos-sre: Actionable triage notes:
- root cause: legacy pairwise feature extraction (O(N^2)) + KV cache thrash under large candidate lists -> increased CPU/GC and worker stalls -> gateway timeout (504) or 502 when connection reset.
- repro steps: run the curl above with candidates=400 and qps ~100+ with concurrent clients. We reproduced locally with `wrk` hitting the endpoint and saw p95 ~8s.

ben-support: Proposed immediate action items:
- maria to push hotfix: server-side hard limit 200 -> responds 413 JSON including \"max_candidates\":200 (ETA 2h)
- amos to add temporary policy in API gateway to return 429 if backend queue depth > threshold (ETA 3h)
- ryan to add SDK advisory note and default jittered exponential backoff in node/python SDKs (ETA 1d)
- infra to increase alerting to include candidate-count dimension

maria-engineering: I'll open a PR for the candidate limit + sampler. Also adding metrics: avg_candidate_count, pairwise_time_ms at request-level.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Started canary for serverside-limit-hotfix on rerank (canary-3)

amos-sre: After canary we should run a load test: wrk with 120 qps, client concurrency 20, candidate list sizes 50/150/400 and verify p95 < 1s for allowed sizes.

elaine-customer: Appreciate the quick response. I'll tell the customer the platform will block >200 candidates and we're tracking a long-term perf refactor.

infra-bot: [alert cleared] api-gateway: 504 spike resolved (since deploy).

ben-support: Follow-up: let's capture a customer incident ticket and CC the customer success rep. I'll own comms.
